summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -3 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates +; dollar 0; brl −; risk 0; energy −; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Rough rice +4.7%; weakest: Lean hogs -18.1%. Key releases ahead: US Core PPI m/m (11-13 8:30 AM ET); US PPI m/m (11-13 8:30 AM ET).

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.98% (-26 bp in a month), 2-year 4.73% (-7 bp); 2s10s curve +25 bp (-19 bp in a month). Falling yields ease funding costs and support commodity investment flows. T-bill yield 4.12% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 103.13 (+0.9% in a month, +4.9% YTD). USD/BRL 5.632 (+13.0% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.662 (-0.5%); USD/MXN 18.61 (+1.9%).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -2.2% in a month (+11.5% YTD); VIX 17.6. Neutral risk backdrop.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 87.41 $/bbl (-6.2% in a month), Brent 94.20, ULSD 4.233 $/gal (-11.4%), natural gas 3.31 (-8.2%). Lower crude weighs on soybean oil and corn through biofuel margins and on cotton via cheaper polyester.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -7.9% in a month, Shanghai Composite -3.8%, Hang Seng -1.4%, yuan +0.5% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 7 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (21%); S&P GSCI -8.3% in a month; gold -7.0%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
